links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under biased patient framing versus standard multiturn consultations
links.effect: Biased consultations reduced accuracy by about 7 to 39 pp across 6 LLMs; ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo fell from 64.0% to 25.0%; bias-influenced error proportion exceeded one-third in all models.
links.quote: ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo declined from 64.0% (SD 0.6%) accuracy in standard consultations to 25.0% (SD 0.9%) under bias (−39.0 pp), and Gemini 1.5 Flash-8B declined from 61.3% (SD 0.7%) to 35.5% (SD 0.6%; −25.8 pp), with both models approaching the 25% random-guess baseline.

links.outcome: Model conformity to patient-preferred incorrect diagnosis (sycophancy-like bias-aligned errors)
links.effect: All 6 models had bias-influenced error proportion above 33.3%; highest 81.0% (ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo), lowest 46.7% (Gemini 1.5 Pro); BIEP and BIAD correlated r=0.97.
links.quote: The strongest conformity occurred in ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo (BIEP=81.0%), whereas Gemini 1.5 Pro showed the lowest alignment (BIEP=46.7%), indicating partial but incomplete resistance to patient bias.

links.outcome: Static single-response benchmark accuracy versus multiturn biased consultation accuracy
links.effect: Static and standard accuracies were comparable (difference ≤6 pp) but biased consultations dropped accuracy sharply, so static benchmarks overlooked the vulnerability.
links.quote: Static and standard accuracies were largely comparable within each model (difference≤6 pp), suggesting that interactive dialogue itself did not substantially affect diagnostic performance in the absence of patient bias.

links.effect: Cognitively biased consultations caused approximately 7 to 39 percentage-point diagnostic accuracy declines.
links.quote: Across all 6 evaluated models, cognitively biased consultations led to marked diagnostic accuracy declines of approximately 7 to 39 percentage points compared with standard multiturn consultations, whereas static single-response tests and standard consultations showed comparable accuracy.

links.effect: Foundation-only models achieved 25.0%‐73.8% accuracy under biased consultations.
links.quote: In biased consultations, the dual-system framework achieved 63.7%‐75.5% accuracy, compared with 25.0%‐73.8% for foundation-only models.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests safeguard practices (prompt-based mitigations, decoding temperature adjustments, and a dual-system conversational vs. reasoning architecture) to counter patient cognitive bias in simulated multiturn clinical consultations.
